harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured daily log rotation for /var/log/inventory/app.log on node1 via /etc/logrotate.d/inventory (daily, rotate 7, compress, copytruncate, missingok, notifempty). Verified the config parses correctly, forced multiple rotation cycles proving compression, 7-rotation retention cap, and continued application writes after rotation via copytruncate. Completed mandatory single-node restart: captured baseline boot_id, rebooted node1 with `shutdown -r now`, confirmed the boot_id changed after reconnect, and verified crond, the logrotate config, and all rotated log data survived the restart.
actions_performed: Inspected node1: RHEL7, logrotate-3.8.6-19.el7 installed, cron.daily/logrotate present and enabled via crond
Dry-ran logrotate -d to confirm config parses with correct 'daily' and '7 rotations' pattern
Forced logrotate -f repeatedly to prove rotation, gzip compression, 7-file retention cap (pruning older files), and that writes to app.log continue uninterrupted after copytruncate rotation
Restored app.log to its original baseline content after testing, leaving the 7 rotated evidence files in place
Captured pre-restart boot_id and service/config/data baseline on node1
Issued backgrounded 'shutdown -r now' via sudo so the ack returned before disconnect
Polled node1 until exec succeeded again, confirming connection timeout during reboot then recovery
Verified boot_id changed post-restart, and confirmed crond active, logrotate config intact, app.log and all 7 .gz rotations intact, and logrotate -d still parses the pattern correctly

evidence.requirement: logrotate config created for /var/log/inventory/app.log: daily, rotate 7, compress, allow continued writes (copytruncate)
evidence.summary: Wrote /etc/logrotate.d/inventory with daily/rotate 7/compress/copytruncate/missingok/notifempty; logrotate -d dry-run confirms correct pattern parsing (daily, 7 rotations)

evidence.requirement: Rotation actually compresses and rotates on demand, and app can keep writing after rotation
evidence.summary: Forced rotation truncated app.log to 0 bytes and produced app.log.1.gz; a write issued immediately after rotation succeeded and appeared in the live file, then a second forced rotation correctly rolled files forward (1.gz->2.gz)

evidence.requirement: Exactly 7 compressed rotations retained, older ones pruned
evidence.summary: 8 forced rotation cycles resulted in exactly app.log.1.gz through app.log.7.gz on disk, confirming rotate 7 retention cap

evidence.requirement: Daily cron mechanism already present to drive rotation automatically
evidence.summary: /etc/cron.daily/logrotate invokes logrotate against /etc/logrotate.conf (which includes /etc/logrotate.d) and crond.service is active/enabled
Captured boot_id 151c4aa9-9e81-4a32-9c22-08c5c441403a, crond active, logrotate config and 7 rotated files present before restart

evidence.requirement: node1 restart acknowledgement returned before disconnect
evidence.summary: Backgrounded 'shutdown -r now' via sudo returned 'reboot issued' immediately

evidence.requirement: node1 boot identity changed (proof of actual restart)
evidence.summary: Connection timed out mid-reboot, then reconnected with a new boot_id a11ab460-a76e-4182-a7f8-55e3f85d2c76, differing from the pre-restart boot_id

evidence.requirement: node1 post-restart recovery of services, config, and data
evidence.summary: After restart: crond active, /etc/logrotate.d/inventory config intact, app.log content intact, all 7 compressed rotation files intact, and logrotate -d still parses the daily/7-rotation pattern correctly
